questions.question: Explain the terms legal personality, unlimited liability and continuity, and state whether a sole trader and a partnership have each.
questions.expected_answer: Legal personality: the business exists in law separately from its owners and can own property, sue and be sued in its own name — neither a sole trader nor a partnership has it. Unlimited liability: owners are personally responsible for all the business's debts, so creditors may claim their private possessions — both have unlimited liability (partners jointly and severally). Continuity: the business continues when an owner dies or leaves — neither has continuity; a sole trader ends with the owner and a partnership dissolves when a partner leaves, dies or joins.

questions.question: Give three advantages and three disadvantages of a sole trader and of a partnership.
questions.expected_answer: Sole trader advantages: easy and cheap to start; quick decisions; owner keeps all profit; personal service; privacy. Disadvantages: unlimited liability; limited capital; owner carries all the work and may lack skills; no continuity. Partnership advantages: more capital; combined skills; shared workload and risk; more viewpoints; easy to start. Disadvantages: unlimited, joint and several liability; disagreements; profit shared; limited capital compared with companies; no continuity.

questions.question: Two partners contribute R30 000 and R50 000. The partnership makes a profit of R160 000. Calculate each partner's share if profit is shared (a) in the ratio of capital and (b) equally.
